editorial:
Imagine a world where dating is a messy game of cat and mouse, and that is exactly what you get here. You follow Harry Myers, a married guy who thinks he can play the field without getting caught. He spends his time flirting and leading a young woman on, thinking he has everything under control. But everything flips upside down when his wife, Isabel Withers, enters the picture. The vibe is light and silly, capturing that classic early talkie energy where the dialogue is snappy and the situations are intentionally ridiculous. It feels like a chaotic comedy of errors where no one is quite as smart as they think they are.

What really makes this work is the funny chemistry between the leads and the weird plot twists. The pacing is quick, though some of the jokes feel a bit dated. You will love the absurdity of the divorce court scene, which is the highlight of the film. If you enjoy old-school slapstick and romantic mishaps, you should definitely give this a go. Since it is an older title, you might want to look for a restored version. Try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to get the best picture quality possible for a film from 1931.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a hilarious twist in the courtroom. Harry tries to get a divorce, but the woman he was flirting with gets hired as a co-respondent to make things difficult for him. Instead of getting his way, Harry ends up caught in his own trap. The chaos leads to a funny realization about loyalty and honesty, and Harry eventually has to make peace with his wife, ending the madness on a light note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic black and white comedies and romantic mishaps.
